Condition: If a workload contains multiple storage-consuming artifacts, represent each applicable component separately before aggregation.

Inputs: Temporary/intermediate dataset generation; preprocessing outputs; scratch requirement
Condition: If the training pipeline creates persistent or scratch data beyond the source dataset, represent that demand separately.

Rule_Name: Inference Model Artifacts Must Be Represented as a Storage Requirement

Inputs: Input data volume; output/artifact volume; persistence requirement
Condition: If input/output data are retained in the storage system being evaluated, include the applicable volumes in the requirement profile.
Output_Decision: Only persisted data within the selected planning scope are counted.

Rule_Name: Storage Devices Must Not Be Aggregated Solely Because They Exist in the Catalogue

Rule_Name: Architecture Must Be Assigned Only From Explicit Architecture Evidence
Rule_Description: Classify a storage candidate as LOCAL_STORAGE, DIRECT_ATTACHED_STORAGE, SHARED_STORAGE, NETWORK_ATTACHED_STORAGE, STORAGE_AREA_NETWORK, DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE, OTHER, or UNKNOWN only when catalogue/source evidence supports the class. If the architecture evidence is insufficient, retain UNKNOWN.
Inputs: Storage_Architecture; Storage_Architecture_Status; Protocol; Storage_Access_Protocol; Host_Interface; Host_Connectivity
Input_Source: Storage catalogue + reconciliation + authoritative architecture sources
Condition: Architecture class lacks explicit evidence
Output_Decision: UNKNOWN until supported; do not infer from product name alone
Source_Title: Storage catalogue and reconciliation baseline; What is NAS (Network Attached Storage) and why is NAS Important?; What Is a Storage Area Network (SAN)?; SNIA Shared Storage Model
Evidence: Architecture classes have distinct access models; catalogue evidence must support classification.
Limitations: Product naming alone can be ambiguous.

Rule_Name: Direct-Attached Storage Must Have an Explicit Host-Attached Path
Rule_Description: A candidate represented as direct-attached is usable through the host only when the catalogue/source evidence identifies a host-attached interface/path such as direct PCIe/NVMe. The architecture label alone is not sufficient if its supporting path evidence is absent.
Inputs: Storage_Architecture; Host_Interface; Host_Connectivity; Protocol; Storage_Access_Protocol
Condition: DIRECT_ATTACHED_STORAGE selected and host path evidence is absent
Source_Title: Storage catalogue and reconciliation baseline; NVMe over PCIe Transport Specification
Evidence: NVMe over PCIe provides a host/SSD transport path; catalogue records Direct PCIe for the six direct-attached candidates.
Limitations: Exact server slot/root-port mapping remains outside this rule.

Rule_Name: Local Storage Must Not Be Assumed To Be Shared
Rule_Description: Storage physically attached to one host must not automatically satisfy storage access requirements of another host. Cross-host access requires an explicit shared/distributed access mechanism or an explicitly modeled replication/caching/staging step.
Inputs: Storage_Architecture; Host_Connectivity; workload node count; shared-access requirement
Condition: One host has local/direct-attached storage but another host requires access
Output_Decision: Do not treat local storage as multi-host accessible without evidence
Source_Title: SNIA Shared Storage Model; 05_Storage_Rules_Part1.csv
Evidence: Direct-attached and shared/network-attached architectures are distinct models.
Limitations: Caching/replication may create a separate access architecture and must be modeled explicitly.

Rule_Name: Shared Storage Requires Explicit Multi-Host Accessibility Evidence
Rule_Description: A storage candidate may be treated as shared/multi-host accessible only when its architecture and access path provide evidence that multiple hosts can access the relevant storage service/pool.
Inputs: Storage_Architecture; Storage_Access_Protocol; Host_Connectivity; Network_Transport; shared-node count
Condition: Multiple hosts require common storage and shared-access evidence is absent
Source_Title: What is NAS (Network Attached Storage) and why is NAS Important?; What Is a Storage Area Network (SAN)?; Storage catalogue and reconciliation baseline
Evidence: Networked/shared storage has explicit host access semantics; not every storage system is automatically multi-host.
Limitations: Actual access control, namespace and client configuration may require deployment-specific validation.

Rule_Name: NAS Classification Requires File-Service Access Evidence
Rule_Description: Classify a candidate as NETWORK_ATTACHED_STORAGE/NAS only when evidence indicates network-connected file access services and an applicable file-access protocol such as NFS/SMB/CIFS.
Inputs: Storage_Architecture; Storage_Access_Protocol; Protocol; Host_Interface
Condition: NAS/file-service classification is claimed without file-access evidence
Source_Title: What is NAS (Network Attached Storage) and why is NAS Important?; Storage catalogue and reconciliation baseline
Evidence: SNIA defines NAS as network-connected storage providing file access services, commonly using NFS/CIFS.
Limitations: Protocol availability alone does not establish complete deployment topology.

Rule_Name: SAN Classification Requires Block-Access Network Evidence
Rule_Description: Classify a candidate as STORAGE_AREA_NETWORK only when evidence indicates a storage network providing block-level access to hosts, with an applicable fabric/protocol path.
Inputs: Storage_Architecture; Storage_Access_Protocol; Protocol; Network_Transport; Host_Connectivity
Condition: SAN classification is claimed without block-access network evidence
Source_Title: What Is a Storage Area Network (SAN)?; Storage catalogue and reconciliation baseline

Limitations: Detailed fabric zoning/path redundancy belongs to later reliability/topology work.

Rule_Name: Write Throughput Feasibility Must Reuse Part 2

Rule_Name: IOPS Feasibility Must Preserve Benchmark Context
Rule_Description: Evaluate required IOPS against candidate IOPS only when request size, read/write mix, queue depth/concurrency and benchmark context are comparable.

Source_Title: Storage Part 2; MLPerf Storage Benchmark Submission Guidelines v2.0

Rule_Name: Latency Feasibility Must Use Applicable Latency Evidence

Rule_Name: Performance Evidence Must Be Comparable Before Hard Failure

Rule_Name: Storage Accessibility Must Reuse Part 3 Architecture Result

Rule_Name: Reliability Requirement Must Reuse Part 4 Protection Decision

Rule_Name: Rebuild and Recovery Dependencies Must Be Evaluated
